outcome_verbatim: Consistent with previous IPS literature, employment was defined as working in a job that paid the legislated minimum wage for a minimum of 1 day in the previous 6-month period.
source_locator: Results, 'Primary outcome - employment status', pp. 78-79: 'the IPS group had a significantly higher rate of having been employed (71.2%, 47/66)'; construct defined in Method, Outcomes, p. 77; denominator corroborated by Results, Participant flow, p. 78 (6-month missingness IPS 9.6%, n = 7, of 73 randomised)
adjusted_measure: odds ratio, IPS v. TAU over 0-6 months, random-effects logistic (xtlogit) model with treatment group, time period, baseline employment and a group-by-time interaction
notes: CONSTRUCT: the report never uses the word 'competitive' and never states the labour-market setting, but the numerator is defined by a legislated-minimum-wage floor, which is the standard operationalisation of competitive employment in the IPS literature the report cites, and IPS is described as designed to return people 'to mainstream employment' (p. 76). It is therefore NOT paid_any: paid work below the minimum wage, which in Australia includes most sheltered and supported-wage employment, is excluded by the definition. Recorded as paid_competitive with the source wording; a reviewer preferring `unclear` has the verbatim to work from (see unresolved_queries.md). HORIZON: 6 months falls in no landmark band (the 12-month band opens at 9 months), so this result cannot enter any horizon. Employment at 6-12 and 12-18 months is reported only as odds ratios, p-values and Fig. 1 predicted probabilities; no count is printed and none is recoverable. ASCERTAINMENT: period prevalence over a stated 6-month window, not point prevalence; one day of paid work in the window suffices. MODERATORS: mean_age and the sex and baseline-employment counts are arm-level baseline values from Table 1, p. 78, on all 73 randomised, not on the 66 observed at 6 months. perc_post_secondary left blank: Table 1 reports highest year of school only (VCE/VCAL 43.8%), which is school completion, not post-secondary education. ADJUSTED EFFECT: 3.40 (95% CI 1.17 to 9.91, z = 2.25, P = 0.025), p. 78; the adjusted model controlling additionally for gender and baseline depression gives 3.57 (95% CI 1.19 to 10.70). adjusted_se left blank rather than reconstructed from the interval.

outcome_verbatim: Currently in paid work (Table 1 row label). Methods: 'Employment status was treated as a binary variable (i.e. employed and unemployed) at baseline and follow-up.'
source_locator: Table 1 'Participant demographics, clinical characteristics, and QoL', Employment status row 'Currently in paid work', Follow-up column (N = 100), p. 773; construct in Materials and methods, Measures, Functioning, pp. 771-772; analysis sample in Results, Sample characteristics, p. 772
notes: WHOLE TRIAL-DERIVED COHORT, BUT NOT PRIMARY-POOL ELIGIBLE, for two independent reasons: the cohort is employment-selected (D9), and the experimental intervention was specifically intended to change employment, which fails the SAP section 2.1 trial-derived safeguard recorded on the arm row. Both are recorded so a reader can see which gate removed it. COUNT VERIFIED INTERNALLY: Table 1 prints 37 (37.00) in paid work and 63 (63.00) not in paid work of N = 100, and Table 4 (p. 775) prints the same total across the three QoL clusters, 13 of 31 + 18 of 48 + 6 of 21 = 37 of 100. CONSTRUCT: coded paid_any because the source's own label is 'currently in paid work' with no restriction on labour-market setting, wage floor or hours. The report gives no definition of the variable, and the parent trial's separate 6-month outcome does carry a minimum-wage floor; see unresolved_queries.md. This is a POINT-prevalence variable ('currently'), distinct from the parent trial's 6-month period measure, and the two are not comparable. DENOMINATOR: the 100 are those with complete 18-month follow-up data, from 145 analysed (146 randomised minus one with missing quality-of-life data). That is attrition and analytic completeness, not post-randomisation subgroup selection (D12.3c). n_assessed left BLANK: killackey2019 reports 102 participants with 18-month data (73 - 17 IPS and 73 - 27 TAU), but that count is from the sibling report and on a different completeness criterion, so it is not typed into this row. MODERATORS: mean_age, n_female and their denominator are the follow-up column of Table 1, i.e. the same 100. n_employed_baseline 24/146 is from killackey2019 Table 1, p. 78 and describes ALL randomised participants, not the 100; clarke2023's own baseline column prints the same 24 but heads the column N = 145 while computing 16.44% on 146 (see inconsistencies.md), so 146 is used as the denominator because it is the base the printed percentage reproduces. HORIZON: 18 months is assigned to t24m under D11.1 (exact tie to the longer horizon).

outcome_verbatim: Patients who during the last year were working half time or more (paid work) were viewed as working. This included working half-time or more for the full year, and working full time for half a year or more. Favorable scores for work were given to those taking care of children or other dependents (often, but not always, women). Patients who were responsible for the welfare of one or more children or other dependents (i.e., a relative needing a live-in caregiver) were scored as working. Patients who kept house only for themselves and/or a live-in partner were not scored as working. Additionally, students who attended school 1/2 time or more were scored as working.
source_locator: Results 3.2, p. 270: 'Thus 9 of 36 patients with schizophrenia prescribed antipsychotics at the 20-year assessments were working (25%) as compared to 16 of the 22 schizophrenia patients not on antipsychotics (73%) (chi-square = 12.683, 1 df, p < .001)'; construct defined in Method 2.3, 'Assessment of work functioning', p. 269; 20-year follow-up denominator in Method, p. 268
notes: CONSTRUCT IS NOT PAID EMPLOYMENT. The score counts three different things as working: paid work at half-time or more, unpaid care of children or other dependents, and attendance at school half-time or more. Paid work below half-time is NOT counted. No paid-employment numerator can be recovered: the report never reports the components separately, so paid_any is bounded only by 0 <= paid_any <= 36 for this group and is not identified (D12.3 reasoning applied to a composite rather than to intensity bands). Coded vocational_activity because the vocabulary's paid_* values all require the numerator to be paid work and paid_or_education would drop the carers. NOT SUMMED ACROSS THE TWO MEDICATION GROUPS: 9 + 16 = 25 of 36 + 22 = 58 would reproduce the manifest's '25/58', and 58 does match the 58 of 70 schizophrenia patients followed at 20 years, but the paper never prints it, the two components sit on different arms and different denominators, and the derived-count rule requires components to share one denominator. MODERATORS: none of mean_age, sex or education is reported for these two subgroups; the sample-level figures (mean age 22.9 years at index, 60% of schizophrenia patients male, median 13 years of education) describe the whole 139 at index hospitalisation, not this subgroup at 20 years, so they are not recorded here. Supplemental Table 1, which gives the other sample characteristics, is cited but not present in the PDF. ARITHMETIC: 9/36 = 25.0%, which reproduces the printed 25% exactly. FOLLOW-UP BASIS: 240 months is elapsed time from the index hospitalisation ('followed up on 5 or 6 subsequent occasions over a 20 year period... at 2 years, 4.5 years, 7.5 years, 10 years, 15 years and 20 years post-index hospitalization', p. 268), so since_baseline, and the horizon is the 108-months-and-above band. ARM: medication status at the 20-year assessment, which is a naturalistic, non-randomised subgroup of the recruited cohort, not an allocated arm and not a separately recruited sample.

outcome_verbatim: Of the 107 participants, 45 (42.1%) were employed at both baseline and follow-up. Current work status was coded as employed or not employed.
source_locator: Results, 'Consistency and Change in Work Status and Benefits and Problems Related to Work', p. 239
notes: COMPONENT ONLY: one cell of the baseline-by-follow-up cross-classification (employed at both assessments). It has no independent analytical meaning as a prevalence and never enters any pool; it exists to make the derived 12-month paid_any count checkable. 45/107 = 42.06%, printed as 42.1%.

outcome_verbatim: Of the 107 participants... 8 (7.5%) were not employed at baseline but were at follow-up. Current work status was coded as employed or not employed.
source_locator: Results, 'Consistency and Change in Work Status and Benefits and Problems Related to Work', p. 239
notes: COMPONENT ONLY: the second cell of the baseline-by-follow-up cross-classification (employed at follow-up but not at baseline). 8/107 = 7.48%, printed as 7.5%.

outcome_verbatim: Current work status was coded as employed or not employed. For current job, information about job title, employer, job duties, hours worked per week, and monthly income were collected. Discussion, limitations: 'the focus of the study was on paid employment and did not explore other comparable areas of role functioning such as household work'.
source_locator: Results, p. 239 (the four cells of the baseline-by-follow-up table and the printed 49.5% at follow-up); construct in Method, Measures, 'Current Work Status, and Benefits and Problems Related to Work', p. 238 and Discussion, limitations, p. 245; denominators in Results, p. 239 and Figure 1, p. 239
derivation_justification: 45 employed at both assessments + 8 employed at follow-up but not at baseline = 53 employed at the 1-year follow-up, of the 107 who completed it. The report prints all four cells of the baseline-by-follow-up cross-classification of the same 107 people: 45 (42.1%) employed at both, 52 (48.6%) employed at neither, 2 (1.9%) employed at baseline only, 8 (7.5%) employed at follow-up only; they sum to 107, so the classification is mutually exclusive and exhaustive on one denominator. The derived count reproduces the report's own printed follow-up rate: 53/107 = 49.53%, printed as '49.5% at follow-up'. The same table gives 45 + 2 = 47 employed at baseline, 47/107 = 43.93%, printed as 43.9% and confirmed by 'Of the 47 participants employed at baseline' on p. 240. This is a sum of printed integer cells, not a back-calculation from a percentage.
checked_by: claude-opus-5 (batch F04): sum and both printed percentages recomputed; INDEPENDENT HUMAN CHECK STILL OUTSTANDING (Stage G)
notes: THE ONLY RESULT IN BATCH F04 THAT REACHES A LANDMARK HORIZON (12 months; interviews were 'conducted between 11 and 13 months following baseline', Method, Procedure, p. 238). ZERO SEPARABLE: the categories are employed and not employed, so zero paid work is a category of its own and is separable from every category containing positive paid work. CONSTRUCT: paid_any. Work status is a binary current-status variable with no wage floor, no hours threshold and no restriction on labour-market setting; monthly income and hours were collected for every employed participant, employer type is categorised as independent employer, family-run business or self-employed, and the paper states that its focus was paid employment. DENOMINATOR: 107 of the 150 enrolled completed the follow-up (71.3%); the 43 lost are itemised in Figure 1 (30 unable to contact, 7 psychiatric hospitalisation, 3 died, 2 declined, 1 missed appointment). Completers differed from non-completers on prior hospitalisation and duration of illness (Results, p. 239), which is recorded for the risk-of-bias assessment and the bounding analyses, not treated as subgroup selection (D12.3c). POPULATION GATE: cohort selection is `none` and the analysed denominator carries no employment restriction, so both D9 gates pass. The cohort will nevertheless be dropped from the primary pool by the diagnosis gate as implemented, because diagnosis_group is smi_mixed and no psychosis-only subgroup employment count is extractable, even though 90% of the sample is schizophrenia-schizoaffective. See unresolved_queries.md; this is a decision for the review team, not something to code around. MODERATORS: n_female 36 of the 107 followed up (Table 1, p. 240). n_employed_baseline 47 of the same 107, from the same cross-classification, NOT the '40%' quoted for all 150, which has no printed count. mean_age left blank: khare2022b prints no age for the 107 (Supplemental Table 1 is cited but not in the PDF); khare2022's mean age of 38.5 years is for its own 133-participant MoCA sample and is not typed here.
